speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether fines meted out to agencies under the Ministry's charge are sufficient deterrence to ensure that unsafe activities are not carried out by the agencies' officers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Government takes workplace safety and health extremely seriously.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) investigates every fatal case thoroughly to ascertain the culpable parties and we will not hesitate to take action against those responsible if wrongdoing is found.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This includes prosecuting the agencies, organisations, culpable senior management and individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Organisations and individuals found guilty under the Act will also suffer reputational damage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Only four countries in the world have achieved this consistently ─ that is the United Kingdom, Netherlands, Sweden and Germany.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: No Asian country has done so on a consistent basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Improving workplace safety and health cannot be achieved through law and punishments alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In addition to a good regulatory framework and putting in place sound policies, it is crucial to build a sustainable workplace safety and health culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This requires a sustained and collective effort by organisations, management, industry associations, union leaders and workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Leaders in the organisations must set the tone and foster a culture and mindset where safety is second nature and where workers feel safe to report unsafe workplace practices to their employers, supervisors or union leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Employers must ensure that their workers are properly trained and equipped with workplace safety and health capability and knowledge; and use technology to detect and prevent workplace accidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Workers themselves must play their part to follow safe work procedures and report unsafe work practices to the appropriate authority.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This ensures their own and their colleagues' safety, so that every worker can return safely home to their loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: On the Government's part, we have implemented various measures and programmes over the years to enhance workplace safety and health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Most recently, the Multi-Agency Workplace Safety and Health Taskforce, or MAST, introduced a series of measures after the Heightened Safety Period, or HSP, to strengthen workplace safety and health ownership and capabilities at the sectoral, company and individual levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For example, we will require Chief Executives (CEs) and Board Directors of all companies in higher-risk industries to attend a programme on how to meet their workplace safety and health responsibilities and develop their companies' workplace safety and health capabilities.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: It is good to hear from the Senior Minister of State that we have got this target in mind, to bring our fatality rates down to 1.0.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And I do hope that we do achieve that consistently in the future.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The one supplementary question that I had was, in terms of the compensation of the office holders who are involved in overseeing workplace safety and health, when there is a public agency involved — because I think the concern here is that, when the public agencies are given the fines, that is obviously fining the public agency.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Then of course, that comes from public funds.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, how do we ensure that the public officers who are in charge, how do they, apart from the usual key performance indicators (KPIs) that ensure they do their jobs well and the usual appraisals, is there an element of compensation that is linked to these safety KPIs?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Is the question more, in terms of whether there is a public sector KPI or —

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: When the public officers are responsible for safety records, is there an element of their compensation or any KPI that is tied to the safety record of the agencies under their charge?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I am not familiar with the individual compensation formulae for Public Service officers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: You may want to try to ask the Public Service Division (PSD) on that one.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: What I am quite certain about is that many of our agencies – in fact, I think all of our agencies – have got a KPI for workplace, safety and health, especially for those overseeing high-risk projects.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is where I am quite familiar  with – many of them have reporting standards and of late, some, for example, like the Land Transport Authority (LTA), have improved their standards by including near-miss reporting, so that they can reduce injury rates.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think you can also seek clarification subsequently, as there is a Ministerial Statement is coming up, on how the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment and National Environment Agency do their tracking.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That is a good example, as well, in terms of how agencies track and monitor their safety records.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I think the Senior Minister of State would know, throughout the years, I have been calling for a dedicated WSH officer for every organisation so that there is a focus on workplace safety.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: And if no, are there any plans – at least for the Public Service – to start having one to focus on some of these projects that have a higher risk, so that risk assessments can be done properly?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Following HSP, as I have shared in my reply earlier, we have set up MAST.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In that team, we have various Ministries who are involved in high-risk projects, where we track performance across not just the sectors, Ministries and contracts, but also the whole sector as a whole.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To some extent, at the management level, there is expectation that they watch this quite closely.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Having said that, that is over a short period of time.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Nonetheless, we look at improving practices as a whole, beyond just having one officer because it is not possible to monitor so many projects across the board.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think it is important that every project is closely watched by the respective project officers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think that makes a difference because they allocate resources, they put the focus, they put the KPIs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That sets the tone and culture; not just at the sectoral or Government level, but across every company.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We need to put that in place to make it sustainable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I wish to elaborate a little bit on a specific case that I believe he is familiar with, about a former investigation officer who was charged with molestation against three women while conducting investigation on behalf of the Health Sciences Authority.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The point I wish to raise is that, that individual who was charged the year before worked for WSH Experts, which is an outsourced agency.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I mentioned this because all individuals, whether contractors or agents directly employed by the Government are subject to the stipulations of the law.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But nevertheless, when this form of law enforcement is outsourced, one wonders, whether these external contractors are put under the same rigours of clearance before employment, because they are after all, carrying out an official duty.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I have to say this is not related to the Parliamentary Question and I think the Member may want to file a separate one.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Generally, I wish to assure Members that as part of Government contracting, there are certain rigours in place.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is not possible to check the character of every single one who comes into contract with the Government, but we do our best to try.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Anyway, if the Member would like more details on the particular case, do file a separate question.
